feedback: Final iteration, so the approved build races unchanged on the unseen track and no later revision can recover a weak candidate. The candidate is the iteration 6 design, the best raced state (255.7). Its geometry is 7 sensors at y = 0.03 m, x = -0.06 to +0.06 m, with weights [-1, -0.75, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1]. The controller is base_speed 1.3, kp 5.0, ki 0.02, kd 0.8, last_direction. Iteration 6 earned 9 of 20 oval finishes with line_loss 0, and every later single-variable test scored lower: y = 0.01 m (iteration 7, 179.1), ki 0.15 (iteration 8, 253.2, no change in max_error), kd 0.5 (iteration 9, 56.8, finishes collapsed), base_speed 1.4 (iteration 10, 192.9, finishes fell from 9 to 4). Lowering base_speed to 1.2 (iteration 5) and widening the sensor array without the inner weights (iteration 4) also cut finishes. The unseen track is the main uncertainty: no design has finished the s-bend or slalom in any race, so the outcome there depends on how the shape of the unseen course interacts with this steering. I am not stating how this candidate will perform. The decision rests on it being the best measured design, and a further revision cannot be tested in time.
requested_changes: No revision is requested: approve the iteration 6 build (base_speed 1.3, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, kp 5.0, y 0.03 m, weights [-1, -0.75, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1]) unchanged. Evidence: it is the best raced design (255.7), and every single-variable change from it (iterations 7 to 10) scored lower.

Do not alter kd, ki, the sensor row or base_speed for the final race. Evidence: kd 0.5 collapsed finishes (iteration 9), ki 0.15 left max_error unchanged (iteration 8), y 0.01 m lowered the score (iteration 7), and base_speed 1.4 lost finishes (iteration 10).

Keep the 7-sensor array at x = ±0.06 m with the inner weights as raced. Evidence: the wider array removed line loss (iteration 4 onward), and the iteration 4 finish loss came from reduced inner weights, which the iteration 5 and 6 weights restored.
